title: Reading evidence — the value of pkit::documentation:reading-evidence, version 1
description: The data point's companion schema (COR-052 point 5; living-docs DEC-001 point 7): the results of executed checks that follow the documentation — a simulated reader running a guide against the system, say. This capability runs no such check; the results arrive from a capability that does, or from the project's own filler file. One entry per result, keyed by three parts — the page or path, the commit and the check: its `id` is `<path>@<commit>#<check>`. So two providers' results for one page at one commit stand side by side, and only two that claim one check collide. The point is `union`, no default takes part, and its inert policy is `fallback`, because the evidence advises: it informs a reader-review and never replaces one (DEC-001 point 6). The version rises only on a change that breaks existing fillers.

commit.description: A commit, by its full hexadecimal name in lower case: 40 digits under SHA-1, 64 under SHA-256. An abbreviated name is refused, so a commit has one spelling.

check-name.description: The name of an executed check: lower-case words of letters, digits and hyphens, joined by dots, the first beginning with a letter (`guide-walker.install-guide`). Underscores, slashes, colons and capitals are refused; the name stands after the `#` of an entry's id.

evidence.description: The result of one executed check, for one page or path at one commit.

id.description: The entry's key, the three parts it is for: `<path>@<commit>#<check>`, the entry's own `path`, `commit` and `check`.

path.description: What the check followed: a page, by its repository-relative path, or a reader path through several pages, by a gitignore-style pattern matching them.

commit.description: The commit the check ran against, by its full name.

check.description: The executed check that gave the result: the name its provider gives it, the same from commit to commit, one per result it reports for a page at a commit — one filler never supplies an id twice, and the whole filler is inert if it does. It opens with the provider's own name: a capability's, or `project` for the project's own (DEC-001 point 7).

outcome.description: `passed`: the reader could follow it. `failed`: they could not.

description.description: One line a person reads: what was checked, and what was found.
